correctness.rationale: The nilpotent upwind shift gives an exact triangular Poisson-convolution formula. Its strictly positive earliest connecting term proves discrete scalar target reachability. Uniform Poisson ratio asymptotics, Stirling, and endpoint Laplace analysis yield the full \(h^4\) exponentially small Gramian equivalent. A centered Poisson positive-part limit and integrable left-tail control give the \(h^{3/2}\) moving-window crossover, and Gaussian integration gives the exact critical constant. The continuum overlap and reciprocal minimum-energy identity follow directly. The packaged checker independently verifies finite semigroup identities and sample asymptotic trends; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The original control-allocation study identifies numerical upwind apparent target controllability without a quantitative mesh cost. The theorem gives exact exponential inflation of the minimum energy before signal arrival and the universal \(h^{3/2}\) onset law. These sharp rates distinguish formal numerical reachability from physically usable controllability and can inform mesh resolution and Gramian threshold interpretation.
